No canary bytes/text/name/hash/crop/repo.detail: A generated canary PDF plus journey values (visible text, hidden Info string, filename, document sha256, pdf base64 head, raster pixel digest, user note + bare token, report id, run key, export filename — 11 greppable markers) was opened through the real built flow in real Chromium: T08 open mount file input → harness page running the real T09 pdf.js adapter (native text + render), the real T10 TesseractOcrReader (staged model download → verify → IDB slot → worker/wasm → occurrences), the real T16 ExportPanel (JSON + HTML Blob/anchor downloads) and the real T22 import mount. Every request URL/method/all headers/post body, response, request failure, websocket, fetch/XHR/beacon/worker/service-worker/WebRTC/WebTransport/form.submit tripwire record, console payload, leg detail, dialog, download and the independent server-side access log (method/path/query/status/request headers) was captured per leg and scanned for every marker in raw, percent, base64, base64url, hex, cross-channel-split and base64-wrapped spellings — first in-test, then again by scripts/inspect_network_receipt.py. 47 requests across 8 captures: zero marker material outbound; the only artifacts containing canary data are the intentional local JSON/HTML downloads and task-private raw captures. Reopened report fetched nothing and executed nothing (no new script/img/network; hostile payload stayed literal text; zero dialogs).

only fixed allowlisted same-origin asset.detail: Inspector checks requests_same_origin (every request netloc == the loopback test origin; zero foreign hosts in requests, egress tripwire, websockets), requests_allowlisted_paths (all 47 requests inside the fixed allowlist: /, index/preview html pages, /assets/*, /models/*, /_headers-adjacent static paths — enumerated in the receipt census), requests_read_only_methods (GET/HEAD only, zero POST/PUT bodies), requests_no_query_strings (zero ? or # on any outbound URL). The staged OCR model fetch is the single warm-path network operation and is allowlisted; warm run proves zero refetch.

telemetry/external-font absence proven.detail: Check no_telemetry_or_external_font scanned every runtime channel for collector/CDN/font-host patterns (sentry, datadog, segment, amplitude, googletagmanager, jsdelivr, unpkg, cdnjs, fonts.googleapis, beacons) — zero hits; no_telemetry check on built assets records the full literal census of external URLs inside the shipped bundles (vendor spec links: tc39.es, whatwg; repo links: github.com; xmlns namespaces: w3.org/xfa.org/adobe; overridden CDN defaults inside vendored tesseract.js; pdf.js parser test vectors) — none are telemetry/collector literals and none appear in runtime traffic. Storage check proves document-free persistence: only the sha256-verified staged model slot (inkflip/models IDB) may persist; local/session storage, CacheStorage and service-worker registrations are empty/absent.

online/warm/offline modes documented.detail: Receipt requires modes cold,warm,offline — 8 captures document all three plus the honestly labeled 'online' setup leg. Cold: shipped index boot (fixed-asset census separated from document data), canary open, full journey incl. real model download (provenance re-derived by the inspector from the wire: exactly one served /models/ fetch). Warm: second run reuses the verified IDB model slot — zero model requests in requests AND server_log. Offline: prepared page completes open→OCR→export with all network blocked — zero server-side hits, zero request failures (browser cache request events for fixed assets are expected and allowed); cold offline context fails specifically as unavailable_offline/missing_model, and cold offline navigation is blocked (no service worker ships — recorded as a limitation). Evidence presence is now REQUIRED (capture_evidence_present): full channel key set, nonempty named legs, storage snapshot, captured request headers, ≥1 request per non-offline capture, journey-leg union coverage — an emptied capture cannot pass.

redact private test logs before public a.detail: Raw captures (tests/privacy/.private/) stay task-private and git-ignored. The inspector writes redacted capture copies (artifacts/tasks/T15/capture/) with every marker encoding replaced by <marker:id> tokens and absolute private paths by <private>; the committed network-receipt.json carries marker ids + sha256_16 digests only — the receipt test asserts marker-freedom of both the receipt and every redacted capture. commands.log redacts the worktree path.

test_summary.runner: python3 scripts/task_acceptance.py run test:privacy (structured-report harness over pinned Playwright Chromium)

limitations: App composition (T13) is not landed: the journey drives the real built feature mounts plus a test-owned harness page in sequence — the same production code paths the composed shell will call.
Browser automation cannot see every OS/browser process channel; per planning, release-profile proof additionally needs a proxy/firewall capture.
No service worker ships: offline support means an already-loaded page with prepared assets, verified here; cold offline navigation has no app shell to load and is not claimed.

WebRTC/WebTransport are tripwired (construction is recorded) and asserted unused across the whole journey — verified absent from the built bundles; an already-open data channel's inner frames are not separately captured, so the guarantee is constructor-level.

Log-channel scans are bounded by capture truncation (console/page-error 2000 chars, leg/egress/dialog details 1000, ws frames 1000); network carriers are closed by method/query/allowlist/header checks, so the residual escape window is log-text only — the inspector additionally scans joined and base64-decoded payloads to shrink it.
